verdict.claim_under_attack: R-B01's recursive normalized-key counsel-assertion scan (counsel_signoff_assertion_present / key_asserts_counsel_signoff / normalized_key_skeleton / fold_confusable in amphora-assurance-capabilities/src/lib.rs) withstands independent adversarial verification with novel encodings beyond the original 8 (A1..A8).
verdict.not_a_safety_breach: fto_status/legal_advice/fto_legal_closure remained correctly pinned (FTO NOT PERFORMED / false / false) in every scenario including V1 and V2, and unresolved_technical_categories still emitted 75 from the live runtime in every scenario -- the module never claims clearance it doesn't have. The refutation is scoped to the detection/recording completeness claim only, exactly as R-B01's own predecessor refutation was scoped.
verdict.root_cause: fold_confusable() only maps a hand-picked whitelist of Cyrillic/Greek homoglyphs to their ASCII look-alikes. Any other non-ASCII letter (e.g. Latin-extended diaeresis forms with no NFKC compatibility decomposition, which are legitimate and common in real candidate text) is NOT substituted -- it is silently DROPPED by the is_ascii_alphanumeric filter in normalized_key_skeleton(). Dropping a letter (rather than mapping it) breaks the substring/token checks that key_asserts_counsel_signoff relies on, so a key that a human reader would immediately recognize as 'signed_by_counsel' or 'counsel_fto' is normalized down to a string that matches neither the canonical name nor >=2 of the 3 semantic token classes, and boolean_counsel_assertion_ignored is wrongly left false. This is a false NEGATIVE on the module's own defensive lock: the module's contract is 'never elevate authority, but always RECORD a candidate-supplied counsel-signoff assertion so it can never be silently ignored' -- V1/V2 show it CAN be silently ignored.
